purpose: Point 5: does the conversation-aware refusal layer (L3) yield a MEASURED leakage reduction, or is it retained as unmeasured defense-in-depth?
method: Exact-match count of _L3_REFUSAL_TEXT firings in existing engine ablation logs (no new model calls). L3 firing = pipeline replaced the response with the L3 refusal constant.

findings.l3_fires_in_isolation: 3/89 turns in C00100 (L3-only), all F2_LINKABILITY multi-turn chains
findings.l3_inert_once_redaction_upstream: 0/89 turns in C01100 (L2+L3, the knee) and 0/89 in C11111 (full): L2 redaction upstream strips the content, so the accumulation threshold is never crossed and L3 never fires.
findings.no_measured_leakage_gain: C01000 (L2 only) and C01100 (L2+L3) judged strict ASR are identical at 0.1923 -> L3 adds no measured leakage reduction over redaction alone. C00100 (L3 only) judged strict 0.3462 is above the 0.2885 baseline (within the 0.08 judged noise floor): no net reduction in isolation either.
findings.conclusion: L3 yields NO measured leakage gain over redaction alone and is effectively inert inside the recommended knee. It is retained only as unmeasured multi-turn defense-in-depth (its sole positive evidence is the constructed handoff unit test in scripts/phase3/l3_tests.py, a co-occurrence that did not arise in the live campaign). The utility/cost table reports full-stack cost (C00000 vs C11111) and does not isolate L3's marginal cost.
